text:
sam: Quick sync: I sketched a "service-spine" decoupling playbook — goal is to move the request-enrichment and tenant-routing logic out of runtime hotpath into an async spine. Wanted quick reactions before I file an RFC.

olivia: Nice. What's the main win?: latency, ownership, or both?

sam: Both. We currently have business logic mixed in the hotpath. Extracted spine would let us iterate on enrichers without touching hotpath code, and we can offload non-critical enrichment to async workers.

kevin: Two risk areas to call out: 1) cross-call latency for enrichment when we keep sync paths, 2) consistency for tenant config lookups.

mara: Also add a SLO for the spine: fraction of requests fully-enriched within 50ms and a second-tier async completion path. If enrichment misses, runtime should fall back to a safe default quickly.

sam: Agreed. My draft phases: 1) thin-proxy facade that forwards to spine while returning defaults for missing enrichments 2) spine implements async enrichment + cache with TTL 3) adopt canary traffic for fancy enrichers 4) migrate critical enrichers to sync path only after perf validation.

kevin: For tenant config, I'd avoid dual ownership. Instead: single source-of-truth service behind a high-throughput cache with short TTL and a streaming updates channel. This avoids heavy reconciliation work.

olivia: Streaming updates need careful backpressure. Make sure the spine has a replayable snapshot API for new nodes.

mara: Operational checklist: rolling restart safe, replay window >= 15m, alert on update-lag > 30s, synthetic tests for enrichment correctness. Also health endpoints per-enricher.

ci-bot: ci-bot: infrastructure test job queued: spine-smoke + enrichment-regressions.

sam: For cutover we propose these guards: - synthetic pipeline pass for 24h - p50 of end-to-end request no worse than +3ms - p99 explained < 8% increase - no unreconciled tenant diffs older than 2 minutes.

kevin: Can we add trace headers that tag whether enrichment was sync/async/missing? That makes postmortems much faster.

olivia: Also require a "graceful-degrade" policy per enricher: ranked fallbacks and quality-weighted scoring so we can measure customer impact during cutover.

mara: I'll pair with Sam to convert this playbook into a runbook with dashboards and alerts. If we get the thresholds right this sounds safe.

sam: Thanks — I'll open an RFC with the phases, runbook, and a mock traffic plan. Will ping the channel when it's up. :rocket:
